spec.body_markdown:
## Velocity: Speed with a Direction

Velocity tells you two things at once: how fast something is moving, and which way it's headed.

**Formula:** v = displacement / time

Because displacement is a vector (it has direction), velocity is a vector too. Compare that to speed, which only cares about distance traveled and never mentions direction.

**Why it matters:** two cars can have the same speed (60 km/h) but very different velocities if one is heading north and the other south. In physics, that difference matters a lot - it changes how forces and accelerations add up.

**Key fact:** if you return to your starting point, your displacement is zero, so your average velocity is zero - even if your average speed was not.
